caption: What if the asteroid that killed the dinosaurs had missed? About 66 million years ago, a rock roughly 10 km wide hit what is now Mexico's Yucatán Peninsula at over 60,000 km/h. The impact wiped out about three quarters of all plant and animal species. If it had missed, dinosaurs, already around for about 165 million years, might have kept ruling. Most mammals back then were small, so our ancestors might have stayed tiny, and humans might never have evolved. No cricket, no samosas. India was an island drifting north at the time, home to Rajasaurus, a meat-eating dinosaur whose fossils were found in Gujarat. The twist: dinosaurs never fully disappeared. Birds are living dinosaurs, and there are about 11,000 species of them, including the pigeon outside your window. Would YOU want to live with dinosaurs? 👇
